skill.name: run_tests
skill.author: Claude Code (Opus) through the Haven MCP executor, task 20261026T230219-f2904f
skill.admission: 5/5 hidden held-out cases, 3/3 dev cases, judged by skills.py (not by the author)

hypotheses.H1: Local models that never saw the skill written succeed on more unseen bug-fix tasks with the executable skill than with tools alone.
hypotheses.H2: The executable skill beats the same procedure given as prose (recipe.md) in the system prompt. If prose matches code, executability adds nothing and H2 is rejected.
hypotheses.H3: With the skill, agents waste fewer commands discovering how to run tests (discovery_waste) and need fewer steps.

arms.recipe: tools + recipe.md in the system prompt

design.task_provenance: Written by the experimenter (Opus, this session) after the brief and before the skill existed; never shown to the skill author; disjoint from dev and held-out admission cases.

outcome_judge: bench/run_bench.py, after the agent finishes: protected test files byte-identical AND the task verifier passes (real pytest 8.3.5 in a private venv, node --test, or unittest). Commit reported separately. The agent's own claims are not used.

decision_rules.H1_supported: skill-arm successes exceed none-arm successes for both agents, summed over tasks
decision_rules.H2_supported: skill-arm successes exceed recipe-arm successes summed over both agents, or tie on success with lower median steps
decision_rules.H3_supported: median discovery_waste and median steps lower in the skill arm than in the none arm
decision_rules.caveat: n=4 tasks x 1 replicate per cell is a pilot. Any effect smaller than 2 tasks is reported as inconclusive, not as support.

known_threats: Tasks are small and synthetic; the experimenter also wrote the brief and the transfer tasks.
t1 imports pytest, which is not installed; the none and recipe arms must build their own runner or install pytest (network is granted, but the sandbox forbids writes outside the repo).
The skill author (Opus) is a far stronger model than the receiving agents; this tests transfer of an artifact, not whether small models can discover skills.
Single replicate at temperature 0; llama.cpp is near-deterministic but not bit-exact across runs.
